# contingency-dsl2procedure

> Compiles a contingency-dsl schedule AST (a plain JSON dict, for example `Conc(VI30s, VI60s, COD=2s)`) into Method-section prose for behavior-analytic papers in JEAB (English) or J-ABA (Japanese) style, with the references it cites collected automatically. Zero runtime dependencies.

contingency-dsl2procedure is part of OperantKit, a set of Python/Rust packages for designing and running operant and respondent conditioning experiments (reinforcement schedules, session recording, analysis). Use it instead of hand-writing Method-section templates: it covers atomic, compound, modifier, second-order, aversive, trial-based, respondent, and multi-phase schedules, writes changeover delay and other parameters as sentences, notes whether components were signaled by discriminative stimuli, and cites primary sources.

## Install

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/OperantKit/contingency-dsl2procedure
```

## Minimal example

```python
from contingency_dsl2procedure import compile_method

ast = {
    "type": "Program", "param_decls": [], "bindings": [],
    "schedule": {
        "type": "Compound", "combinator": "Conc",
        "components": [
            {"type": "Atomic", "dist": "V", "domain": "I", "value": 30.0, "time_unit": "s"},
            {"type": "Atomic", "dist": "V", "domain": "I", "value": 60.0, "time_unit": "s"},
        ],
        "params": {"COD": {"value": 2.0, "time_unit": "s"}},
    },
}
method = compile_method(ast, style="jeab")  # or style="jaba" for Japanese
print(method.procedure)
# Responses were reinforced under a concurrent VI 30-s VI 60-s schedule. A 2-s changeover delay was in effect.
print([ref.key for ref in method.references])  # ['fleshler_hoffman_1962', 'herrnstein_1961']
```

`compile_method` returns a `MethodSection` with `subjects`, `apparatus`, `procedure`, and `references`; `method.to_text()` renders the whole section as Markdown. `compile_paper` handles multi-experiment `Paper` roots. The `contingency-dsl2procedure INPUT [--style jeab|jaba] [--output PATH]` command does the same from a JSON file or stdin. To start from DSL text, produce the dict with `to_dict(parse(source))` from contingency-dsl-py.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/OperantKit/contingency-dsl2procedure/blob/main/README.md): install, 30-second example, why not to hand-roll a generator, usage
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OperantKit/contingency-dsl2procedure/blob/main/AGENTS.md): when to use this package and what not to do

## Related packages

- [contingency-dsl](https://github.com/OperantKit/contingency-dsl): the schedule language specification and its AST schema
- [contingency-dsl-py](https://github.com/OperantKit/contingency-dsl-py): parses DSL text into the AST dict this package reads (`pip install contingency-dsl-py`)
- [contingency-procedure2dsl](https://github.com/OperantKit/contingency-procedure2dsl): the reverse direction, Method-section text to AST (`pip install git+https://github.com/OperantKit/contingency-procedure2dsl`)
- [contingency-py](https://github.com/OperantKit/contingency-py): runs the same schedule as a reinforcement schedule engine (`pip install contingency-py`)
